title: A Harbor for the Tide
premise: Ansel Marchetti has spent ten years raising his daughter alone in the coastal town of Greywater, hiding his heart behind the counter of the only bookshop, convinced love is a discipline he can out-train. When a freak snowstorm traps him overnight with Julian Voss—the rival who broke his heart in their twenties and is now back to buy the harbor district for a development firm—and Priya Nair, the town archivist fighting to save it, old wounds and older feelings resurface. As Ansel's daughter's custody arrangement with her late wife's family comes due, he must finally speak the sentence he rehearsed for a decade: that he chooses love, and himself, over safety. In the end, Julian walks away from the deal, Priya wins the archive battle, and Ansel opens the bookshop door—to both of them.
about_author: Sable Okafor is a former lighthouse keeper's assistant turned novelist who writes love stories set in towns where the sea keeps everyone honest. They live on the Atlantic coast with two cats and an unreasonable collection of tide charts.

chapters.title: The Weight of Ordinary Mornings
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. We meet Ansel opening Tidebound Books, making breakfast for his daughter Wren, and cataloging his life like inventory—everything in its place, nothing left to chance. A letter from the Harrow estate about custody arrives; he files it unopened. Emotional beat: controlled calm masking dread.

chapters.title: A Stranger with Familiar Hands
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Julian Voss walks into the bookshop after ten years, all city tailoring and easy charm, scouting properties for Meridian Development. Their banter is barbed and electric. Ansel pretends not to remember everything. Emotional beat: shock sharpened into armor.

chapters.title: What the Archive Keeps
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya Nair discovers Meridian's plans would raze the harbor archive, including records of the town's founding families—including Ansel's late wife's. She confronts the town council and finds Julian charming the room. Emotional beat: righteous anger meeting an immovable opponent.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Rehearsed Sentences
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, flashback-woven. The night Julian left for London, and the sentence Ansel never said. Present-day: Wren asks why her father looks at Mr. Voss 'like a math problem.' Emotional beat: grief for a younger self who stayed silent.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian justifies the development as salvation for a dying town, but Ansel's cold courtesy rattles him more than any protest. He requests a site survey during the winter festival week—a choice he can't explain. Emotional beat: ambition curdling into doubt.

chapters.title: The Festival of Lanterns
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The town rallies at the lantern festival; Priya and Ansel form an alliance against Meridian. Julian appears anyway, and Wren—unaware—befriends him over caramel apples. Emotional beat: community warmth tightening around three secrets.

chapters.title: Forecast: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A historic snowstorm hits early. Roads close, power flickers, and Priya arrives seeking shelter just as Julian's car dies outside the shop. Three rivals, one bookstore, no exits. Emotional beat: the trap closing gently, like snowfall.

chapters.title: One Night, Three Truths
chapters.summary: Rotating POV by section. Trapped overnight, they play Wren's truth-or-dare by candlelight. Priya reveals she came to Greywater fleeing a career built on other people's erasure; Julian admits the project was supposed to feel like winning. Emotional beat: defenses thawing faster than the storm.

chapters.title: The Best Mistake of Our Twenties
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. With Wren asleep, Julian and Ansel finally name what happened ten years ago—and what almost did. A near-kiss interrupted by the power returning. Emotional beat: desire and terror in equal measure.

chapters.title: Morning After the World Changed
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Snowplows come; so does reality. Julian leaves for a board call, promising nothing. Priya catches Ansel smiling at the door and realizes she isn't the only one falling. Emotional beat: fragile hope exposed to daylight.

chapters.title: Custody Papers and Other Weapons
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The Harrows invoke the custody clause: if Ansel remarries or cohabits, they'll contest full guardianship, citing instability. His lawyer confirms the threat is real. Emotional beat: the past weaponized against the future.

chapters.title: Julian's Ledger
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. In the city, Julian falsifies nothing but omits much, delaying the demolition timeline. His mentor warns him sentiment is a liability. Julian starts a private ledger of what Greywater actually costs. Emotional beat: conscience becoming arithmetic.

chapters.title: An Alliance of Convenience
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya and Ansel dig through the archive and find the harbor deed contains a public trust clause that could block Meridian entirely—if they can prove continuous community use. Emotional beat: purpose replacing heartbreak, briefly.

chapters.title: Wren's Question
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Wren, sharp-eyed at eleven, asks if Julian is the man from the photograph hidden in her father's desk drawer. Ansel lies badly. That night he writes the rehearsed sentence and burns it. Emotional beat: a father learning honesty is inherited.

chapters.title: The Board Vote
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Meridian's board accelerates demolition to outrun the trust clause discovery. Julian must present the site report—or sabotage it. He submits a version that understates feasibility, knowing it will end his career. Emotional beat: betrayal of ambition in favor of something unnamed.

chapters.title: Exposed
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Julian's doctored report leaks; the town hails him a hero while Priya suspects the truth is worse—that he lied to them all along, heroism included. She confronts him publicly. Emotional beat: admiration collapsing into fury.

chapters.title: The Sentence, Finally Spoken
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. At the custody hearing, asked whether his life is stable, Ansel says the rehearsed sentence aloud: 'I have loved the same person for ten years, and I am done pretending that loving people is a risk I can manage.' Emotional beat: the decade-long dam breaking.

chapters.title: What It Costs to Stay
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Fired and unmoored, Julian returns to Greywater intending to apologize and leave. Instead he finds Ansel's burned sentence reconstructed by Wren from the ash edges, taped inside a first edition. Emotional beat: devastation discovering it was witnessed.

chapters.title: The Trust Clause Hearing
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya presents decades of festival records, fishing licenses, and Wren's own school essays about the harbor as evidence of continuous use. The clause holds; Meridian withdraws. Emotional beat: small-town memory defeating corporate forgetting.

chapters.title: Three People, One Doorway
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel tells Priya the truth: his heart chose years ago, but there is room in it the way there is room in a harbor—for more than one ship. Priya, who has always chosen herself, decides to stay anyway. Emotional beat: love refusing scarcity.

chapters.title: Spring Tide
chapters.summary: Rotating POV. Months later: the custody agreement is renegotiated with the Harrows won over by Wren's happiness; the archive becomes a living museum with Priya as director; Julian signs on to restore the wharf instead of demolishing it. Emotional beat: every thread knotted into place without being tied too tight.

chapters.title: A Harbor for the Tide
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, final chapter. Closing time at Tidebound Books. Wren does homework among the shelves, Priya catalogs upstairs, Julian argues happily with a customer about tide charts. Ansel locks the door, leaves the light on. Emotional beat: arrival—the heart, trained at last, in the direction of home.
